last_debrief: STORY SO FAR: Sun 07-26 — a STORY DAY on the kel/kitta toggle, low dose, and the catch axis finally moved in-session. Opened on the fielding knock he answered COLD off the lock screen that morning (maami's 'innoru thadava saapidunga' -> 'Illa, vayiru full') and paid it off with the -iduchu completive tail: nirainjiduchu, hooked to வந்துடுச்சு which he had STOLEN off his wife and sister on 07-24 without knowing what the tail was. He liked the machine but did NOT fire it — asked twice for 'vayiru ___' and both times answered 'full' in English. FIRST CONTACT ONLY; teach beat done, demand it next time, do not treat as a miss. THE CATCH WIN: ran a full-speed aththai/akka gossip tape (youknow-la opener planting Vasanthi by name, ennamo prachanai, alaichal, -nu sollraanga, theriyala) and he caught the drift clean — aththai has gossip, prachanai at somebody's house, reported second-hand, Chennai back-and-forth, and he glossed ALAICHAL correctly as 'very busy' unprompted. Three never-taught words in a native-speed tape and the drift survived. Two recasts: (1) theriyala read as 'I know' — it is the NEGATIVE, theriyum+illa, and it is HIS OWN -la engine (saapidala/puriyala/mudiyala) not firing in a new verb; watch this, the -la tail is productive but not yet automatic in comprehension. (2) kalyanam NIKKAADHU — he got the reported frame but missed the payload (the marriage is falling through). He did NOT name the referent even though the opener planted it — frame:youknow-la still uncaught, still the load-bearing catch item. MY BUG, owned to him: the tape used 'appa' (அப்ப, then/so) and he read it as appaa (father). Phonetic collision — do not put அப்ப in a phonetic tape again. THE TOGGLE LANDED, both directions in one exchange: 'maami-kitta ketten' fired COLD instantly on a novel person, and person-less 'hall-la ketten' = I HEARD it came back with the verb right and the case wrong (hall-ku, dative-for-locative) plus verb-before-place order; he self-corrected to hall-la ketten on the recast. First miss of the sequence was reaching for SOLLU (akka solaa) when asked to ASK — the ask/tell confusion is upstream of the kitta switch, worth one more strain. yaaru? TAUGHT today (unseen -> seen), framed as the repair for his own 07-25 referent-hunting instinct; demand it next time. STUDIO/ENGINEERING RESIDUE, all his to handle in @build: run_studio.py's agy writer failed lint twice (996-char stub + FOURTH WALL, it named Andrew as a speaker) so M75 went to the studio subagent, which produced clean at 54s and pushed 63f3636 — I misread its 1:27pm intermediate commit as a truncated render and told him there was a render bug; there is not, and I corrected it in-session. Four untracked mission76 artifacts are sitting in his tree. THE OVERHEAR WEEK IS STILL NOT AGREED — pitched 07-24, raised twice today, he answered neither time (he answered 'story day' to the shape question and skipped the campaign question). Today RAN its shape anyway (catch headline + kel/kitta fire riders) and it worked. Ask ONCE more at the next open; if he skips it a third time, stop asking and just run it. STANDING CATCH ORDER still live and unrenewed today. Still unanswered from 07-24: 'wande' and 'velam' — asked for surrounding sentence twice now, no answer; drop them if he skips again. Replies shortened to fragments by the end — he was done, and was let go, same as Friday. DENSITY LOW, LORE HIGH still holds: two fires and one gossip tape produced more than any gauntlet.

soak_order.scene_seed: The completive tail: an aththai who will not accept that anything is finished — the rice is eaten, the bus has gone, the marriage fell through — every closed fact answered with -iduchu until she gives up
soak_order.focus: A conjugation carousel over three roots — the endings are the lesson, the words are just the carrier. (1) போ: போறேன் / போவேன் / போறோம் / போவோம் / போனேன் / போனோம் / போகணும் — same root, person and tense moving underneath it. (2) முடி for finishing: முடிஞ்சிடுச்சு / முடியல / முடியாது / முடிஞ்சா. (3) the DONE tail, -ஆச்சு and -இடுச்சு: நேரம் ஆச்சு / சாப்பிட்டாச்சு / வந்துடுச்சு / நிறைஞ்சிடுச்சு. Andrew has met all of these; none is reflex. Put the forms back to back so the tails separate by ear.
